title: Jaffar Express hijacking
description: On March 11, 2025, Balochistan Liberation Army militants stopped the Jaffar Express near Sibi in Balochistan, Pakistan, hijacking roughly 400 passengers inside a railway tunnel and executing many during a standoff that lasted into the next day; at least 64 people were killed, including 33 militants and 31 civilians and security personnel, before security forces killed the remaining attackers and freed 354 hostages.

title: Air India Flight 171 crash
description: On June 12, 2025, Air India Flight 171, a Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner bound for London, crashed into the student hostels of B. J. Medical College in Ahmedabad about 32 seconds after takeoff and 1.7 km from the airport; 241 of the 242 people on board and 19 people on the ground were killed, in the first fatal accident involving a Boeing 787.

title: IRGC claims retaliatory strike on US base in Kuwait amid Iran war
description: On July 31, 2026, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it had targeted a US base in Kuwait in retaliation for American strikes on Iran, after an earlier Iranian attack on a building in Kuwait housing a Chinese company had killed one person the previous day. The strikes were part of the sharp escalation of the 2026 Iran war following the resumption of US bombardment of IRGC targets in Iran on July 29; no further casualty figures for the Kuwait attack had been released at the time of reporting.

title: Flash floods and landslides in Dien Bien Province
description: Flash floods and landslides struck Dien Bien Province in the early hours of 1 August local time, killing at least 10 people and injuring seven. The disaster damaged homes and roads in Tia Dinh and Xa Dung communes and isolated several villages; heavy rain also flooded parts of Son La Province.

title: Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv
description: Russian forces launched a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv shortly after midnight on 1 August local time, killing at least nine people and injuring more than 20, including children. Fires broke out across four districts and rescue operations continued through the night.

title: Terrorist attack on labourers in Kulgam
description: Unidentified terrorists opened fire on two labourers from Chhattisgarh at a brick kiln in Kulgam district, killing one and injuring the other. Authorities said the attack targeted non-local workers.

title: Calabar flood and landslide crisis
description: Weeks of torrential rain in July 2026 caused flooding and landslides across Calabar, killing at least 10 people, including a baby swept away by floodwater and a father buried in mud. The rains destroyed homes, triggered landslides that killed families, and cut off access roads; the toll was cumulative through the end of July.

title: Abiemnom massacre
description: On 1 March 2026, several hundred armed youths from Unity State crossed into Abiemnom County in South Sudan's Ruweng Administrative Area and attacked the town for about three hours, killing 169 people — 79 government soldiers and 90 civilians — and wounding 68. More than 1,000 residents took shelter in the UNMISS compound during the attack; officials attributed it to rebel-linked militias, though attribution remained disputed.

title: Russia launches massive missile and drone strike on Ukraine
location: Kyiv, Lviv and Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine
description: In the early hours of July 30, 2026, Russia launched one of its largest combined strikes of the war, firing dozens of ballistic and cruise missiles and hundreds of drones (President Zelensky cited over 70 missiles and 280 drones) at cities across Ukraine, with damage reported from east to west in Kyiv, Lviv and Kryvyi Rih. At least 10 civilians, including children, were killed and more than 50 injured, including six people killed by a ballistic missile strike on Kryvyi Rih and a family of six killed in a village hit by a suspected North Korean missile; NATO scrambled jets in response and a stray Russian cruise missile briefly entered Polish airspace.

title: Avalanche on Broad Peak leaves climbers missing, four confirmed dead
description: An avalanche swept ten climbers from the 8,051-metre Broad Peak in the Karakoram on July 30, 2026, leaving them reported missing, among them celebrated Nepalese mountaineer Nirmal Purja and Omani climber Nadhira Al Harthy. Rescue teams recovered the bodies of four of the climbers by July 31, while helicopters continued to search for the remaining six in one of the deadliest mountaineering accidents on the eight-thousander in recent years.

title: Coal mine explosion in Balochistan
description: A methane gas explosion ripped through a coal mine in Balochistan province on 30 July, killing at least 34 miners. Rescue officials recovered 32 bodies and said two workers remained trapped in an inaccessible section of the mine.

title: Sudan famine confirmed in North Darfur camps
description: In February 2025, the United Nations confirmed famine conditions in at least five areas of Sudan, including the Zamzam, Abu Shouk and Al Salam displacement camps in North Darfur and two locations in the Western Nuba Mountains. The Sudan Doctors Union estimated in January 2025 that about 522,000 children had died from malnutrition since the civil war began, amid widespread aid access restrictions imposed by the warring parties.

title: Myanmar earthquake (magnitude 7.7)
description: On March 28, 2025, a magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck near Sagaing and Mandalay in Myanmar along the Sagaing Fault, collapsing buildings and infrastructure and also killing 18 people in Bangkok, Thailand. Myanmar's military government reported about 3,770 dead, while independent Myanmar media estimates exceeded 5,000, and the true toll was widely considered higher.

title: New Orleans Bourbon Street truck attack
description: On January 1, 2025, Shamsud-Din Jabbar drove a pickup truck into crowds celebrating New Year on Bourbon Street, then opened fire, killing 14 people and injuring dozens before being fatally shot by police. The FBI classified the attack as a terrorist act inspired by the Islamic State, to which Jabbar pledged allegiance in videos posted before the attack.

title: Angara Airlines Flight 2311 crash
description: On July 24, 2025, Angara Airlines Flight 2311, an Antonov An-24 turboprop, crashed roughly 16 km from Tynda airport in Amur Oblast, Russia, while landing in poor weather; all 42 passengers and 6 crew members on board died.

title: Gul Plaza shopping mall fire
description: On 17 January 2026, a fire broke out at the Gul Plaza shopping mall in Karachi, Pakistan, killing at least 79 people and injuring more than 20. The blaze engulfed the multi-storey commercial building, and many victims died trapped in shops and offices; it was among the deadliest building fires in Pakistan's recent history.

title: West Bandung landslide
location: West Bandung Regency, West Java, Indonesia
description: On 24 January 2026, heavy rainfall triggered a major landslide in West Bandung Regency, West Java, Indonesia, that buried the village of Pasir Langu and killed at least 74 people, with others missing. Rescue operations in the mud-covered area continued for days as dozens of homes were destroyed.

title: Afghanistan flash floods
description: In late April 2025, heavy rains triggered flash floods across northern Afghanistan, with the worst destruction in Baghlan Province, where entire villages were swept away; at least 150 people were killed across the affected provinces per BBC reporting, while the World Food Programme estimated more than 300 dead and hundreds more injured.

title: Qinyuan coal mine explosion
description: On 22 May 2026, an explosion at the Liushenyu coal mine in Qinyuan County, Shanxi Province, China, killed at least 82 miners, the worst coal-mining blast in China in more than a decade. The blast in one of China's major coal-producing regions prompted a state investigation into safety practices.

title: Kumamoto earthquake
description: On 28 July 2026, a magnitude 6.8 earthquake (M7.1 on the Japanese scale) struck Kumamoto Prefecture on the Hinagu Fault, killing 36 people and injuring 129. The second floor of Aeon Mall Kumamoto collapsed and later exploded, a chimney collapse at a paper factory in Yatsushiro killed nine workers, and about 10,000 people were displaced, with the Kyushu Shinkansen damaged at more than 200 locations.

title: Syrian coastal massacres of Alawites
description: From March 6, 2025, security forces and allied armed groups linked to Syria's caretaker government carried out a crackdown that turned into mass sectarian killings of Alawite civilians in the coastal governorates of Latakia and Tartus, as well as parts of Hama and Homs, in response to an insurgency by Assad loyalists; death toll estimates range from about 1,000 to 2,000, with a Reuters investigation documenting at least 1,479 Alawites killed on March 7-9.

title: Nigeria fuel tanker explosion in Suleja
description: On January 18, 2025, a fuel tanker exploded at the Dikko junction near Suleja in Niger State after a crash, engulfing people who had gathered to collect spilled fuel; Nigeria's Federal Road Safety Corps confirmed more than 100 bodies were recovered and buried, with dozens of others badly burned.

title: Kwara State attacks
description: On 3–4 February 2026, hundreds of Boko Haram gunmen of the Sadiku faction surrounded the villages of Nuku and Woro in Kaiama, Kwara State, near the Beninese border, killing at least 162 people in door-to-door executions, with the toll later reported to exceed 200. Attackers blocked exits, torched homes, shops and the palace, shot people who answered a mosque call to prayer, and kidnapped 38 others; the dead included the chief imam, a school principal and schoolchildren.

title: South Korea wildfire outbreak
description: Between March 21 and May 15, 2025, wildfires across central and southern South Korea, the largest starting in Uiseong County, destroyed thousands of buildings and killed at least 32 people, making it the deadliest wildfire outbreak in the country's recorded history.

title: Shooting of Minnesota state legislators
description: In the early hours of June 14, 2025, a gunman attacked the homes of Minnesota Democratic state legislators in the Minneapolis suburbs, fatally shooting Representative Melissa Hortman and her husband at their Brooklyn Park home and wounding Senator John Hoffman and his wife; the suspect was arrested and later pleaded guilty to murder.

title: M23 capture of Goma
location: Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: Between January 23 and 30, 2025, Rwandan-backed M23 rebels captured Goma, the capital of North Kivu province in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, after heavy fighting against the national army, UN and SADC peacekeepers, and allied militias; the UN estimated about 2,900 people were killed and another 2,900 wounded, with hundreds of thousands displaced.

title: Islamabad mosque suicide bombing
description: On 6 February 2026, a suicide bomber detonated explosives at the Khadija Tul Kubra Mosque, a Shia mosque in the Tarlai Kalan area of Islamabad, Pakistan, during Friday prayers, killing at least 31 worshippers and injuring more than 100. It was the deadliest attack in Islamabad in nearly a decade.

title: Los Angeles wildfires (Palisades and Eaton fires)
description: From January 7 to 31, 2025, wind-driven wildfires devastated Los Angeles County, most destructively the Palisades Fire in Pacific Palisades and the Eaton Fire in the Altadena-Pasadena area, destroying more than 16,000 structures and killing at least 31 people, one of the deadliest and most destructive wildfire events in California history.

title: 2026 Venezuela earthquakes
description: On 24 June 2026, a doublet of earthquakes — an Mw 7.2 foreshock followed roughly 30 seconds later by an Mw 7.5 mainshock — struck the central Venezuelan coast, with epicenters in Yaracuy state and offshore La Guaira state. At least 5,546 people were killed and 16,740 injured, with tens of thousands initially missing; nearly 800 buildings collapsed and about 590,000 were damaged, and the worst-hit communities in La Guaira lost roughly 80% of their buildings. The UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction estimated US$37 billion in direct damage.

title: Kocani nightclub fire
description: On March 16, 2025, pyrotechnics used during a concert ignited flammable acoustic foam in the unlicensed, overcrowded Pulse nightclub in Kocani, North Macedonia, producing a rapidly spreading fire and toxic smoke; 59 people were killed at the scene and the final death toll reached 63 as injured victims died in hospital, with about 193 injured.

title: Gamo Zone floods and landslides
description: On 10 March 2026, days of heavy rainfall in the Gamo Zone of South Ethiopia triggered widespread flash floods and landslides that killed at least 125 people. The disaster struck farming communities in the southern highlands, destroying homes, roads and farmland across multiple villages.

title: Jilli market airstrike
description: On 11 April 2026, a Nigerian military airstrike hit a crowded market in Jilli, Yobe State, killing more than 100 civilians; authorities described the strike as a misfire. It was one of the deadliest airstrike incidents in Nigeria's counterinsurgency campaign in 2026 and drew calls for independent investigations into civilian casualties.

title: Mindanao earthquake
description: On 8 June 2026, a magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck offshore Sarangani province, Mindanao, on the Cotabato Trench, killing at least 106 people (107 per final tallies) and injuring 1,320, with 7 missing. More than 121,000 homes were damaged or destroyed and damage exceeded ₱71 billion (US$1.44 billion). General Santos, Sarangani, South Cotabato and Davao Occidental were hardest hit, and coastal uplift of up to 2 metres damaged marine habitats across Sarangani Bay.

title: Rubaya coltan mine collapse
location: Rubaya, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: On 28 January 2026, a landslide at the informal coltan mines in Rubaya, North Kivu, killed more than 400 miners and diggers, with some reports placing the toll higher. The collapse occurred amid a surge of artisanal mining in the conflict-affected region, and a second collapse at the same mines on 3 March 2026 killed at least 200 more people.

title: Balochistan Liberation Army attacks
description: Between 29 January and 5 February 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Army launched a coordinated series of attacks across Balochistan province, Pakistan, including raids on a police station and banks in Kharan, a security post in Panjgur and military positions in Harnai. The week-long campaign left at least 225 people dead, including 36 civilians and 2 security personnel, while Pakistani forces reported killing 216 militants in retaliatory raids.

title: Potomac River mid-air collision (American Airlines Flight 5342)
description: On January 29, 2025, American Airlines Flight 5342, a PSA Airlines regional jet arriving from Wichita, collided mid-air with a US Army Black Hawk helicopter over the Potomac River while on approach to Reagan Washington National Airport; all 67 people aboard both aircraft died, making it the deadliest US aviation accident since 2001.

title: Unity oilfield plane crash
description: On January 29, 2025, a Beechcraft 1900D operated by Eagle Air on behalf of Light Air Services crashed shortly after takeoff from the Unity oilfield airstrip in Unity State, South Sudan, while carrying oil workers to Juba; 20 of the 21 people on board were killed.

title: Tumbler Ridge school shooting
description: On 10 February 2026, an 18-year-old former student shot and killed her mother and 11-year-old half-brother at their home in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, then entered Tumbler Ridge Secondary School and shot six people before dying by suicide, for a total of nine dead and 27 injured. It was the deadliest mass shooting in Canada since the 2020 Nova Scotia attacks and the deadliest school shooting in the country since 1989.

title: Gaza war ceasefire
description: A ceasefire between Israel and Hamas took effect on January 19, 2025, after 15 months of war in which the Gaza Health Ministry reported more than 47,000 Palestinians killed and most of the territory's population displaced. The first phase of the agreement included releases of hostages and prisoners before hostilities later resumed.

title: Antioch High School shooting
description: On January 22, 2025, 17-year-old Solomon Henderson opened fire in the cafeteria of Antioch High School in Nashville, Tennessee, fatally shooting one student and wounding another before killing himself with a self-inflicted gunshot; police said he fired ten rounds in about 17 seconds.

title: Bahia Blanca flash floods
description: On March 7-9, 2025, roughly 290 mm of rain fell within hours over Bahia Blanca, Argentina, triggering catastrophic flash flooding that killed at least 17 people and forced mass evacuations; the floods were described as the worst in the city's recorded history.

title: Israel-Iran war (Twelve-Day War)
description: On June 13, 2025, Israel launched Operation Rising Lion, striking Iranian military and nuclear facilities and killing commanders and nuclear scientists; Iran responded with more than 550 ballistic missiles and over 1,000 drones fired at Israel over 12 days. Roughly 33 people were killed in Israel and about 1,060 in Iran, according to the respective authorities.

title: Militant drone-and-ambush attack on police checkpoint in Hangu
description: Militants, blamed by police on the Pakistani Taliban (TTP), launched a drone strike and ambush on the Khazina Banda police checkpoint in Hangu district on the evening of July 29, 2026, in an assault that also involved an attack on a neighbouring checkpost. Eleven police officers, including a deputy superintendent of police, were killed as the death toll rose through the following morning, with initial reports citing 9 to 10 officers dead and at least 28 injured; authorities said 15 attackers were also killed in the ensuing gunfight. It was the second major assault on security forces in the area within a week amid escalating attacks in the Afghanistan–Pakistan border region.

title: US–Saudi airstrikes kill 20 Iran-backed militiamen in Iraq as US strikes on Iran resume
description: As part of the 2026 Iran war, US Central Command and Saudi forces carried out joint strikes on positions of Iran-backed militias in Iraq on July 29, 2026, killing 20 Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) militants, including several Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) members, according to the PMF. The same day, after a six-day pause, the US military resumed heavy waves of strikes against dozens of IRGC targets inside Iran in retaliation for an attempted missile attack on US forces in the Middle East a day earlier, an escalation that prompted Iranian retaliatory strikes on Kuwait days later.
sources: Wikipedia: July 2026 United States strikes against Iran

title: Wildfires in southern Greece kill three firefighters
location: Rethymno, Crete and Gytheio, Laconia, Greece
description: During a late-July heatwave that fuelled wildfires across southern Greece, three firefighters were killed on July 29, 2026 — two while battling a fire near Rethymno on the island of Crete and one near Gytheio in Laconia in the Peloponnese. The fires, part of the broader 2026 European heatwaves, forced the evacuation of thousands of people on Crete and destroyed farmland, olive groves and residential areas before crews brought the blazes under control in early August.

title: Firefighting helicopter crash in San Juan kills seven
description: A Bell 412 helicopter leased by Argentina's Federal Emergency Management Agency crashed on July 29, 2026, in the Ischigualasto natural park in San Juan Province while on a training flight before deployment to firefighting operations in the neighbouring La Rioja Province. The aircraft lost contact with ground control at about 10:26 a.m. local time, and all seven people on board — firefighters, police officers and civil protection personnel — were killed in the crash, which was one of Argentina's deadliest aviation accidents in years.
